projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The steady rise in connected devices from 14 to 17 between 15:44 and 17:06 aligns with typical after-school arrival times, indicating the children have returned and are settling indoors. This stationary indoor occupancy explains the lack of camera motion triggers, but the complete absence of camera logs alongside high presence confirms the home is occupied while highlighting a potential camera health or privacy mode issue.

Despite a stable presence of 14-16 connected devices and a recent spike to 16, the cameras have logged zero activity in the last 4 hours, suggesting a potential camera system outage, network issue, or privacy mode that is disabling motion detection while the house is actively occupied.

The synchronized drop to 14 connected devices at 11:12 AM, followed by a stable count and zero camera activity for over two hours, strongly indicates a planned departure that bypassed motion detection. This aligns with a typical Tuesday afternoon schedule, with no signs of return yet.

The steady decline in connected devices from 16 to 14 over the past hour, paired with zero camera activity, suggests a gradual departure from the home. This likely indicates a family member has left for work or school, though door or garage sensors would confirm.

The transient drop to 15 devices at 08:38 followed by an immediate return to 16, combined with the stable 16-device count since 07:12, points to a routine morning transition (likely a family member heading to the garage or car for school drop-off) rather than a connectivity glitch or security concern.

At 07:12 AM, the connected mobile device count increased from 15 to 16 without any corresponding camera activity or alerts, suggesting an unannounced arrival or device connection that went unnoticed. This warrants a quick check to confirm it's a routine family member or guest rather than an unexpected visitor.

The drop from 16 to 15 connected devices at 01:11 AM, paired with zero camera activity and the late hour, indicates the group has settled in for the night with one person or device disconnecting, consistent with normal late-night winding down rather than an active event.

The stabilization of the device count at 16 combined with zero camera activity at 12:02 AM indicates the household is settled indoors for the night, confirming the earlier device spike was likely just late arrivals rather than an active gathering or security event.

The number of connected devices unexpectedly jumped from 14 to 16 at 22:30, suggesting new arrivals or devices connecting late on a Monday night. This warrants attention as it breaks the stable pattern and lacks corresponding camera activity to verify the event.

Two mobile devices disconnected from the home network between 19:28 and 19:34, indicating recent departures. This confirms a shift in household occupancy and aligns with typical evening routines, so no action is needed.
